name: Ilorin

summary.text: Ilorin was settled first by Yoruba from Oyo, and for a time by Bariba. It grew as a military post of the Oyo Empire until Afonja, Oyo’s field marshal, rebelled in 1817 with the help of the Fulani preacher Shehu Alimi; Alimi’s line took the town, and Ilorin became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate under Gwandu. Its four quarters are still Hausa, Yoruba, Fulani and Yoruba Muslim.

founders.text: The first settlers came from Oyo; Afonja, the Kakanfo, made it his base.
Shehu Alimi (Salih Janta), a Fulani scholar, came from Oyo with Yoruba Muslims; his descendants are the emirs.
Bariba lived at Ilorin for many years and left, for no known reason.

under.text: A provincial military settlement of the Oyo Empire.
An emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate, under Gwandu.

reviewNotes: The year the emirate began (shown as 1824) needs a written source.
